concerns_addressed: Verified T1 scope files directly: lib/resolve-temp.js, lib/format.js, tests/resolve-temp.test.js, tests/format.test.js
Confirmed task deliverables: registry-based resolveTemp path, LOCALAPPDATA fallback, sizeHuman formatting, and documented contract shape
Confirmed no out-of-scope changes beyond the 4 specified files

strengths: Read-only invariant is preserved: no fs.writeFile, fs.unlink, fs.rm, spawn, or destructive exec in lib/
Only permitted read-only exec is execFile('reg', ['query', ...]) in lib/resolve-temp.js
resolveTemp fallback logic is correct: registry result -> %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp -> process.env.TEMP -> C:\Temp
Contract shape is clearly documented in JSDoc in lib/format.js (Entry fields + status enum)
sizeHuman implements exactly requested behavior for verified cases: '0 B' exact, base 1024, 1 decimal for GB case
Tests cover the 4 GWT scenarios from the task packet: registry success, registry fallback, sizeHuman zero, sizeHuman 2.5 GB
Tests are realistic and safe: stub registry/query injection used, no live file system or registry mutation

issues.description: Registry parser regex is hard-coded to REG_EXPAND_SZ; if Local AppData is stored as another REG_* type, parser silently misses it and uses fallback. Not spec-breaking, but slightly fragile in edge environments.

Non-zero byte lengths are formatted with decimals even when value is an integer. The task packet examples do not forbid this, but it creates outputs like '512.0 B' for exact byte values, which is stylistically unusual.
sizeHuman coverage is valid but narrow: only 0 and one large GB value are asserted. Mid-range boundary cases such as 1023, 1024, 1025, KB/MB thresholds are not covered.
